subproblems.title: Countable-radius formula for the upper limit at 0⁺
subproblems.statement: For every function f : ℝ → [0,∞], the upper limit of f along the filter 𝓝[>]0 of right neighbourhoods of 0 equals inf over n ∈ ℕ of sup over t ∈ (0, 1/(n+1)) of f(t): limsup_{t→0⁺} f(t) = inf_{n∈ℕ} sup_{0<t<1/(n+1)} f(t).
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent-supplied proof (P. Mattila, Geometry of Sets and Measures in Euclidean Spaces, Thm 18.5, Mickle–Radó), which uses ϑ(c) = inf_q g_q(c) "by the definition of limsup". This child proves that identity for an arbitrary [0,∞]-valued function, with q = n + 1.

Notation. f : ℝ → [0,∞] is arbitrary. 𝓝[>]0 is the filter of right neighbourhoods of 0 (sets containing an interval (0,ε) with ε > 0). For ε ∈ ℝ put G(ε) := sup_{t∈(0,ε)} f(t) ∈ [0,∞] (so G(ε) = 0 when ε ≤ 0).

1. Basis formula. The intervals (0,ε), ε > 0, form a basis of 𝓝[>]0 (Mathlib `nhdsGT_basis 0`; ℝ has no largest element). For a filter with a basis (s_i)_{p i} and a function u into a complete lattice, limsup u = inf_{i, p i} sup_{a∈s_i} u(a) (Mathlib `Filter.HasBasis.limsup_eq_iInf_iSup`). Hence limsup_{𝓝[>]0} f = inf_{ε>0} G(ε).
2. Monotonicity of G. If ε ≤ ε′ then (0,ε) ⊆ (0,ε′), so every value f(t) occurring in the supremum G(ε) also occurs in G(ε′). Hence G(ε) ≤ G(ε′) (Mathlib `biSup_mono`).
3. First inequality. For each n ∈ ℕ we have 1/(n+1) > 0, so ε = 1/(n+1) is admissible in step 1 and inf_{ε>0} G(ε) ≤ G(1/(n+1)). Taking the infimum over n gives inf_{ε>0} G(ε) ≤ inf_{n∈ℕ} G(1/(n+1)).
4. Second inequality. Let ε > 0. By the Archimedean property of ℝ there is n ∈ ℕ with 1/(n+1) < ε (Mathlib `exists_nat_one_div_lt`). By step 2, inf_{m∈ℕ} G(1/(m+1)) ≤ G(1/(n+1)) ≤ G(ε). Since ε > 0 was arbitrary, inf_{n∈ℕ} G(1/(n+1)) ≤ inf_{ε>0} G(ε).
5. Conclusion. By steps 1, 3 and 4 and antisymmetry, limsup_{𝓝[>]0} f = inf_{n∈ℕ} sup_{t∈(0,1/(n+1))} f(t). In Lean notation this is `limsup f (𝓝[>] 0) = ⨅ n : ℕ, ⨆ t ∈ Ioo 0 (1 / ((n : ℝ) + 1)), f t`. ∎

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent-supplied proof (Mattila, Thm 18.5): inner continuity on balls makes c ↦ ψ(B(c,τ)) lower semicontinuous, and g_q is a supremum of lower semicontinuous functions. Here this is proved for every truncation radius r ∈ ℝ.

Notation. k := m + 1. ℝᵏ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with Euclidean distance |·|. B(c,τ) = {z : |z − c| < τ} is the open ball (empty when τ ≤ 0). For t > 0, tᵏ denotes the extended real ENNReal.ofReal(tᵏ), which lies in (0,∞); quotients are taken in [0,∞]. A function h : ℝᵏ → [0,∞] is lower semicontinuous when, for every c and every a < h(c), some neighbourhood U of c satisfies a < h(c′) for all c′ ∈ U. The hypothesis (H) is ψ(B(c,τ)) = sup_{τ′∈(0,τ)} ψ(B(c,τ′)) for all c ∈ ℝᵏ and τ ∈ ℝ.

1. For every τ ∈ ℝ, the map c ↦ ψ(B(c,τ)) is lower semicontinuous. Fix c and a ∈ [0,∞] with a < ψ(B(c,τ)). By (H), a < sup_{τ′∈(0,τ)} ψ(B(c,τ′)). By the definition of the supremum there is τ′ ∈ (0,τ) with a < ψ(B(c,τ′)); in particular 0 < τ′ < τ (Mathlib `lt_biSup_iff`). Since τ − τ′ > 0, U := B(c, τ − τ′) is an open neighbourhood of c. Let c′ ∈ U and z ∈ B(c,τ′). Then |z − c′| ≤ |z − c| + |c − c′| < τ′ + (τ − τ′) = τ, so B(c,τ′) ⊆ B(c′,τ). By monotonicity of the outer measure ψ, a < ψ(B(c,τ′)) ≤ ψ(B(c′,τ)) for every c′ ∈ U. This is lower semicontinuity at c, and c was arbitrary.
2. For every t ∈ (0,r), the map h_t(c) := ψ(B(c,t))/tᵏ is lower semicontinuous. Since tᵏ ∈ (0,∞), the map φ(x) := x/tᵏ is a strictly increasing bijection of [0,∞] onto itself, with inverse y ↦ y·tᵏ. It is continuous (Mathlib `ENNReal.continuous_div_const`, as tᵏ ≠ 0) and monotone (Mathlib `ENNReal.div_le_div_right`). Directly: if a < φ(ψ(B(c,t))), then a·tᵏ < ψ(B(c,t)). By step 1 there is a neighbourhood of c on which a·tᵏ < ψ(B(c′,t)), i.e. a < φ(ψ(B(c′,t))). (In Mathlib: `Continuous.comp_lowerSemicontinuous` applied to φ and step 1.)
3. A pointwise supremum of lower semicontinuous functions is lower semicontinuous. Suppose a < sup_{t∈(0,r)} h_t(c). Then a < h_t(c) for some t ∈ (0,r). By step 2, a < h_t(c′) ≤ sup_{s∈(0,r)} h_s(c′) for all c′ in a neighbourhood of c (Mathlib `lowerSemicontinuous_biSup`). Hence c ↦ sup_{t∈(0,r)} ψ(B(c,t))/tᵏ is lower semicontinuous. If r ≤ 0 the index set is empty and the function is identically 0; the argument covers this case too. ∎

subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, k := m+1, ψ an outer measure on ℝᵏ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), K ⊆ ℝᵏ closed with ψ(K) = 0, C ∈ [0,∞] and r ∈ ℝ such that ψ(B(z,τ)) ≤ C·τᵏ for all z ∈ K and all 0 < τ < r (B open balls). Then for every c₀ ∈ K and every real t with 0 < t and 6t ≤ r: ψ(B(c₀,t))·Lᵏ(B(0,1)) ≤ C·6ᵏ·Lᵏ(B(c₀,2t)∖K). Here Lᵏ is Lebesgue measure, τᵏ means ENNReal.ofReal(τᵏ), and arithmetic is in [0,∞] with 0·∞ = 0.

Source: step 3 of the parent-supplied proof (Mattila, Thm 18.5, Mickle–Radó), namely the chain ψ(B(c₀,t)∖K) ≤ Σ_iψ(B(z′_i,6d_i)) ≤ q6ᵏΣ_id_iᵏ = q6ᵏω_k^{−1}Σ_iLᵏ(B(z_i,d_i)) ≤ q6ᵏω_k^{−1}Lᵏ(B(c₀,2t)∖K). Here it is stated for an arbitrary constant C in place of q and an arbitrary admissible radius r in place of 1/q. The parent obtains the bound 6d_i < 1/q from d_i ≤ 2ε^{1/k}t. This child uses instead d_i ≤ |z_i − c₀| < t, which the parent also proves, together with 6t ≤ r.

Notation. k := m + 1. ℝᵏ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with Euclidean distance |·|. B(x,ρ) is the open ball. Lᵏ is Lebesgue measure (`volume`). ω := Lᵏ(B(0,1)). For ρ ≥ 0, ρᵏ in [0,∞] means ENNReal.ofReal(ρᵏ). Arithmetic is in [0,∞], with 0·∞ = 0. Hypotheses: ψ is an outer measure (monotone and countably subadditive); K is closed with ψ(K) = 0; C ∈ [0,∞]; r ∈ ℝ; (B) ψ(B(z,τ)) ≤ C·τᵏ for all z ∈ K and 0 < τ < r; c₀ ∈ K; and t ∈ ℝ with 0 < t and 6t ≤ r.

0. Facts used. (a) For x ∈ ℝᵏ and ρ ≥ 0, Lᵏ(B(x,ρ)) = ρᵏ·ω. This is the scaling of the additive Haar measure Lᵏ (Mathlib `Measure.addHaar_ball`), with finrank_ℝ ℝᵏ = k (Mathlib `finrank_euclideanSpace_fin`). (b) K is nonempty, because c₀ ∈ K.
1. Removing K. Put T := B(c₀,t)∖K. Since B(c₀,t) ⊆ T ∪ K, subadditivity gives ψ(B(c₀,t)) ≤ ψ(T) + ψ(K) = ψ(T).
2. Radii. For z ∈ ℝᵏ let d(z) := dist(z,K) = inf_{y∈K}|z − y| (Mathlib `Metric.infDist`). Let z ∈ T. Then: (i) d(z) > 0, because K is closed and nonempty and z ∉ K (Mathlib `IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos`); (ii) d(z) ≤ |z − c₀| < t, because c₀ ∈ K and z ∈ B(c₀,t) (Mathlib `Metric.infDist_le_dist_of_mem`); (iii) B(z,d(z)) ∩ K = ∅, because every y ∈ K has |z − y| ≥ d(z) (Mathlib `Metric.disjoint_ball_infDist`).
3. Vitali selection. Apply the Vitali covering lemma for open balls (Mathlib `Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_ball`) to the index set T, the centres z ↦ z, the radii d, the radius bound R := t (valid by 2(ii)) and the enlargement factor 5 > 3. It gives u ⊆ T such that the balls B(b,d(b)), b ∈ u, are pairwise disjoint, and every a ∈ T has some b ∈ u with B(a,d(a)) ⊆ B(b,5d(b)).
4. Countability of u. The balls B(b,d(b)), b ∈ u, are open, nonempty (they contain b, by 2(i)) and pairwise disjoint in the separable space ℝᵏ. So u is countable: each such ball contains a point of a fixed countable dense set, and distinct indices give distinct points (Mathlib `Set.PairwiseDisjoint.countable_of_isOpen`).
5. Recentring on K. K is closed and nonempty in the proper space ℝᵏ. So for every b ∈ ℝᵏ we may choose z′_b ∈ K with |b − z′_b| = d(b) (Mathlib `IsClosed.exists_infDist_eq_dist`). If |y − b| < 5d(b), then |y − z′_b| ≤ |y − b| + |b − z′_b| < 5d(b) + d(b) = 6d(b). Hence B(b,5d(b)) ⊆ B(z′_b,6d(b)). Now let a ∈ T. Then a ∈ B(a,d(a)) because d(a) > 0. By step 3, B(a,d(a)) ⊆ B(b,5d(b)) ⊆ B(z′_b,6d(b)) for some b ∈ u. Therefore T ⊆ ⋃_{b∈u} B(z′_b,6d(b)).
6. Bound on each enlarged ball. Let b ∈ u ⊆ T. By 2(i)–(ii), 0 < 6d(b) < 6t ≤ r, and z′_b ∈ K. So (B) gives ψ(B(z′_b,6d(b))) ≤ C·(6d(b))ᵏ = C·6ᵏ·d(b)ᵏ.
7. ψ-estimate. By step 5, monotonicity, and countable subadditivity over the countable index set u (Mathlib `measure_biUnion_le`), then step 6:
 ψ(T) ≤ ψ(⋃_{b∈u}B(z′_b,6d(b))) ≤ Σ_{b∈u} ψ(B(z′_b,6d(b))) ≤ Σ_{b∈u} C·6ᵏ·d(b)ᵏ = C·6ᵏ·Σ_{b∈u} d(b)ᵏ.
8. Volume estimate. Let b ∈ u and y ∈ B(b,d(b)). Then |y − c₀| ≤ |y − b| + |b − c₀| < d(b) + t < 2t by 2(ii), and y ∉ K by 2(iii). So B(b,d(b)) ⊆ B(c₀,2t)∖K. These balls are pairwise disjoint Borel sets indexed by the countable set u. By fact 0(a), countable additivity of Lᵏ (Mathlib `measure_biUnion`) and monotonicity:
 (Σ_{b∈u} d(b)ᵏ)·ω = Σ_{b∈u} Lᵏ(B(b,d(b))) = Lᵏ(⋃_{b∈u}B(b,d(b))) ≤ Lᵏ(B(c₀,2t)∖K).
9. Conclusion. Multiplication by a fixed element of [0,∞] is monotone. Also (Σ_b x_b)·ω = Σ_b (x_b·ω) and Σ_b (a·x_b) = a·Σ_b x_b for nonnegative extended reals (Mathlib `ENNReal.tsum_mul_right`, `ENNReal.tsum_mul_left`). Using steps 1, 7 and 8:
 ψ(B(c₀,t))·ω ≤ ψ(T)·ω ≤ C·6ᵏ·(Σ_{b∈u} d(b)ᵏ)·ω ≤ C·6ᵏ·Lᵏ(B(c₀,2t)∖K).
 This holds for every C ∈ [0,∞]. If T = ∅ then u = ∅, all sums vanish, and ψ(B(c₀,t)) = 0. ∎

Source: step 3 of the parent-supplied proof (Mattila, Thm 18.5, Mickle–Radó). The parent takes a Lebesgue density point c₀ of the compact set K, fixes ε = 1/(2q²12ᵏ) and t₀, and derives ψ(B(c₀,t)) ≤ tᵏ/(2q) from the Vitali chain. Here the same estimate is run with ε ↓ 0, which shows that the upper density vanishes at every such density point. Sibling used: vitali_bound (Lean `Submission.rectifiability_mickle_rado_vitali_bound`).

Notation. k := m + 1. ℝᵏ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k). B(x,ρ) is the open ball and B̄(x,ρ) the closed ball. Lᵏ = `volume`. ω := Lᵏ(B(0,1)). For t > 0, tᵏ means ENNReal.ofReal(tᵏ) ∈ (0,∞). Arithmetic is in [0,∞]. Hypotheses: ψ is an outer measure; K is closed with ψ(K) = 0; C ∈ [0,∞) (C ≠ ∞); r > 0; (B) ψ(B(z,τ)) ≤ C·τᵏ for all z ∈ K and 0 < τ < r. Claim: for (Lᵏ⌞K)-a.e. c, limsup_{t↓0} f_c(t) = 0, where f_c(t) := ψ(B(c,t))/tᵏ.

1. Choice of good points. ℝᵏ is a finite-dimensional normed space, so it is a second-countable metric space with the Besicovitch covering property, and Lᵏ is locally finite. Lebesgue's density theorem in the form of Mathlib `Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div` (applied to Lᵏ and K) gives, for (Lᵏ⌞K)-a.e. c, R_c(ρ) := Lᵏ(K ∩ B̄(c,ρ))/Lᵏ(B̄(c,ρ)) → 1 as ρ → 0⁺. Since K is closed, hence Borel, (Lᵏ⌞K)-a.e. c lies in K (Mathlib `ae_restrict_mem`). Fix c ∈ K with R_c(ρ) → 1 as ρ → 0⁺.
